description: AI candidate with inflated claims: 'custom vector database', 'RLHF reward model reduced hallucination 80%', 'multi-agent platform from scratch'. Tests: does the interviewer dig into the technical specifics behind impressive-sounding but hollow AI claims?

config.role_context: LLM-powered product features; RAG pipelines and agent orchestration

persona.name: Daniel Cross
persona.summary: Polished, impressive-sounding AI leader. His CV is a highlight reel of every trending AI term but the specifics are hollow. Knows genuine team management and basic ML pipelines; inflates everything else.

project_knowledge.cv_item: Team leadership at Nexus AI (managed 8 people — genuinely)
can_explain: Hiring, sprint planning, introduced CI/CD. The team DID ship. His role was real — just not the technical architect he claims.

project_knowledge.cv_item: Basic ML pipelines at DataCorp (churn, fraud)
can_explain: Standard sklearn pipelines, some XGBoost. The 45% recall improvement was mostly from adding more features, not a novel ensemble.

hollow_claims.cv_claim: Implemented a custom vector database optimized for multi-modal embeddings, achieving sub-10ms retrieval at 100M+ document scale
hollow_claims.reality: They use pgvector with IVFFlat. There is no custom DB — 'sub-10ms' is a pgvector benchmark he read, not something he measured or achieved.
hollow_claims.under_probing: When asked for specifics on the index: "we used a standard approach -- HNSW-type indexing tuned for our workload." Does NOT name specific parameters or tools. When pressed for measurement: "the infra team validated the latency targets." Cannot describe how. If pressed again: "I wasn't directly involved in the benchmarking -- I designed the architecture."
hollow_claims.deflection_style: Emphasises 'custom' and 'from scratch'; pivots to 'we evaluated several options' without naming them.

hollow_claims.cv_claim: Designed and trained a reward model for RLHF that reduced hallucination by 80% across all deployed models
hollow_claims.reality: He read about RLHF. Never implemented it. No model was fine-tuned with RL. The '80% reduction' was a thought experiment he shared with the team after reading the InstructGPT paper.
hollow_claims.under_probing: When asked how hallucination was measured: "we had an evaluation framework -- standard practice for RLHF." Does NOT name the metric, annotation process, or tool. When pressed: "I'd need to pull up the exact methodology -- the team has detailed docs on it." If pressed again: "My role was more on the model architecture side than the evaluation design."
hollow_claims.deflection_style: Textbook definition of RLHF, then pivots to 'the real win was aligning the model with user intent'.

hollow_claims.cv_claim: Architected and deployed a multi-agent LLM orchestration platform serving 50K+ daily requests with 99.9% uptime
hollow_claims.reality: It's a simple router that sends prompts to different models based on keyword matching. No agent-to-agent communication, no tool use, no planning. 'Multi-agent' means 'multiple different prompts'.
hollow_claims.under_probing: When asked about routing architecture: "standard pub-sub approach with a central orchestrator." Cannot explain failure modes or handoff protocol. When pressed on numbers: "that was our peak traffic -- monitoring confirmed it." Cannot describe the monitoring setup. If pressed again: "the SRE team owned the metrics -- my focus was architecture."
hollow_claims.deflection_style: Describes it as 'proprietary' when pressed on architecture details.

hollow_claims.cv_claim: Fine-tuned Llama-3-70B on a proprietary dataset of 5M+ enterprise documents, achieving state-of-the-art results
hollow_claims.reality: He ran a single LoRA fine-tune on 500 documents with default parameters. No hyperparameter sweep, no evaluation against baselines, no 'state-of-the-art' comparison. The 5M figure is the size of the raw corpus, not what was actually used.
hollow_claims.under_probing: When asked about the fine-tuning setup: 'standard LoRA fine-tune — we used the HuggingFace PEFT library.' Cannot name the LoRA rank or training hyperparameters. When pressed on evaluation: 'we compared outputs against a held-out test set.' Cannot describe the evaluation methodology or what baseline they compared against. When pressed on 'state-of-the-art': 'within our enterprise domain, the results were very competitive.' Cannot name any external benchmark. If cornered on the 5M figure: 'that was the total corpus size — the actual training set was a curated subset.'

persona.answering_style:
Opens confidently with fluent AI vocabulary. First answers sound authoritative but are light on specifics.

ESCALATION UNDER PROBING (FAST):
- When asked for a specific: give a VAGUE answer immediately. "We had a standard evaluation pipeline," "the team ran benchmarks," "we used the usual tooling." Do NOT invent specific-sounding details.
- When pressed again ("what tool?"): deflect to the team. "I'd need to check with the infra team for the exact setup -- I was more on the architecture side."
- When pressed a third time: admit it. "Honestly, I wasn't directly involved in running those benchmarks. My focus was the high-level design."

Key rule: NEVER name a specific tool, framework, or methodology when probed on inflated claims. Stay vague -- no invented benchmarks, no fake evaluation pipelines.

stage2_criteria.name: Smooth interview arc
stage2_criteria.conversation_goal_prompt: The interview follows arc: greeting → get-to-know → CV deep-dive → technical probing → wrap.

stage2_criteria.name: Drills into AI architecture claims
stage2_criteria.conversation_goal_prompt: CV claims: custom vector DB (sub-10ms at 100M+), RLHF reward model (80% hallucination reduction), multi-agent platform (50K req/day), fine-tuned Llama-3-70B (SOTA). PASS if the interviewer asks mechanism-level follow-ups ('what index structure?', 'how did you measure hallucination?', 'how do agents communicate?') on AT LEAST 2 of these claims.

stage2_criteria.name: Probes measurement methodology for bold numbers
stage2_criteria.conversation_goal_prompt: The CV contains many quantified claims (50K requests, 99.9% uptime, 80% reduction, 10ms, 5M documents, 45% recall). PASS if the interviewer asks 'how was that measured?' or 'what metric?' for at least 1 claim.

stage2_criteria.name: Gap becomes visible
stage2_criteria.conversation_goal_prompt: By the end, at least one exchange shows a specific question receiving a vague or circular answer, making the gap observable in the transcript.

sim_user.end_instruction: Participate fully. When wrap-up comes, ask about the AI stack, then call [END_CALL].
